messages.subject: Nonlinear regression with INLA
parts:
Hi all,

I’m trying to use INLA for a nonlinear regression with t-Student residuals, but I’m stuck as I don’t know how to specifiy the regression function.

This is a simplified R-INLA code :

n=100
a = 1
b = 3
s2 = 1.5
z = rgamma(n,2,3)
eta = a*exp(1-exp(-z/b))
tau = 1/s2
y = rnorm(n, mean = eta, sd = 1/sqrt(tau))
data = list(y=y, z=z)
formula = ?
result = inla(formula, family = “T", data = data,
              control.family = list(...)
              )
summary(result)

Is it possible to fit this model with INLA?  If the answer is yes, could you provide a clue on how to do it.

Any help is appreciated
Cheers

Hi,
The only nonlinear model available in INLA for now you can see from
 inla.doc('sigm')
Elias

So, I suggest the structured random effects. You loose the interpretability of the parameters in the parametric nonlinear models but gain a lot in flexibility.

Elias
